findings.evidence: Lean formally refuted the displayed equality chain. For the logistic sigmoid σ'(kz) = σ(kz)(1−σ(kz)) exactly, so σ'(kz)/k = σ(kz)(1−σ(kz))/k, not σ(kz)(1−σ(kz)) — the factor $1/k$ is dropped in the final simplification. Witness $k = 2$, $z = 0$: the chain gives $1/8 = 1/4$, which is false. The surrounding text says the surrogate is divided by $k$ (i.e. $(1/k)\cdot \tfrac{d}{dz}\sigma(kz) = \sigma(kz)(1-\sigma(kz))$), so the first equality $\sigma'(kz)/k$ is the slip. Confined to the appendix formalisation; the main-text fast-sigmoid analysis (Eq 5) and the empirical results are unaffected.

The claim that the sigmoid surrogate satisfies $\tilde{\sigma}'_k(z) > \sigma'(z)$ 'for most $z$' is sign-reversed. Since $\sigma'(u) = e^u/(1+e^u)^2$ is even and strictly decreasing in $|u|$, for $k > 1$ and $z \neq 0$ we have $\sigma'(kz) < \sigma'(z)$, so the normalized surrogate $\sigma'(kz)$ (or $\sigma'(kz)/k$) *shrinks* gradient magnitudes rather than growing them, and the asserted 'positive bias in gradient magnitude, $\text{bias} = \mathbb{E}[\partial\tilde{L}/\partial W - \partial L/\partial W] > 0$' does not follow from the stated premise. The qualitative conclusion is rescued only by the main-text fast-sigmoid surrogate $1/(1+k|x|)^2$ (Eq 5, Lean-PASSED), which is genuinely larger than $\sigma'(x)$ for most $x$; the appendix's sigmoid analysis has the wrong sign.

summary: All 14 self-contained mathematical objects extracted and checked: 2 via formal Lean 4 proofs (run strictly serially against one shared project, MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper), 12 via informal review. Lean PASSED the fast-sigmoid surrogate derivative identity (Eq 5, the only closed-form calculus claim in the main text) and REFUTED the appendix's surrogate-gradient equality chain $\tilde{\sigma}'_k(z) = \sigma'(kz)/k = \sigma(kz)(1-\sigma(kz))$: the factor $1/k$ is dropped ($k=2,z=0$ gives $1/8 \neq 1/4$). All main-text definitions (objective Eq 1, LIF soft-reset Eq 4, cosine similarity Eq 6, adaptive slope Eq 7, reward Eq 8/9) and the backpropagation formulas in §8.1 are well-formed with no algebraic errors; the §8.3 energy computation recomputes to 97416.704 pJ ≈ 9.7×10⁻⁵ mJ, matching the reported value. Two minor errors were found, both in the supplementary §8.1 formalisation of gradient alignment: (1) the surrogate equality chain missing the $1/k$ factor (Lean-refuted, confidence 0.95), and (2) the claim $\tilde{\sigma}'_k(z) > \sigma'(z)$ 'for most $z$' has the wrong inequality direction for the sigmoid surrogate, so the 'positive bias' conclusion is unsupported (confidence 0.82). Neither error invalidates the paper's main empirical claims (slope–magnitude–alignment tradeoff, TD3BC+JSRL results) nor the correct main-text fast-sigmoid analysis (Eq 5); they affect only the appendix's supporting formalisation.
